unit.title: Мобильные игры: сенсорный ввод и виртуальное управление

learning_outcomes.statement: Covers touchscreen and multi-touch input, the design demands of on-screen virtual controls, and the abstraction of a 'game action' decoupled from the physical input that triggers it.

evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: Covers touchscreen and multi-touch input, the design demands of on-screen virtual controls, and the abstraction of a 'game action' decoupled from the physical input that triggers it.

A touchscreen can report several simultaneous contact points, unlike a desktop mouse event. -- Confirmed -- accurate; `pygame.mouse.get_pos()` returns a single tuple and `get_pressed()` a 3-tuple of buttons, consistent with the contrast drawn.
Virtual controls must be finger-sized, must not occlude important screen area, and stay responsive. -- Confirmed -- standard, correct mobile UX guidance, illustrated by a real rendered mock-up.

Separating action from input lets the same game logic serve keyboard, gamepad and touch. -- Confirmed -- the schematic `dejstvie_nazhato("prygok")` is sound, and 20.20 later maps it onto real constants including `pygame.JOYBUTTONDOWN` (verified to exist, value 1539).
